skill.effect: The creature suddenly surges forward with frantic energy, its turbine heart pounding loudly enough to betray its location. As it races, the frantic beating weakens nearby targets.

chains.weakness: Heart overheats if burst is used too long; must rest to cool.
observe: Chest pulses visibly with starfish pattern
Wings beat in rapid, synchronized strokes
Blood flow visible through translucent skin near heart

journal.en: Flyers don't need brains; they have hearts that pump like pistons and wings that sing.

plausibility.summary: Highly speculative Qu organ—reframe in play as extreme avian-grade four-chamber heart with enlarged cor pulmonale flow and supplemental anterior air-sac oxygen shunt (dense 22% O₂), not literal starfish morphology; overheating weakness maps to sustained anaerobic burst at high wing loading.

links: Open skies and varied thermal updrafts favor maneuverability

skill.effect: When it remains still, the creature steadily climbs higher into the air, its stretched wing membranes catching the updrafts. Its elevated position makes it difficult to track and strike.

chains.weakness: Cannot land on narrow branches; crashes on complex terrain.

journal.en: They do not fly; they negotiate with the sky.
